_comment: Golden baseline of the 114C.5 human-account route policy -- a SEPARATE
fixture from role_policy_baseline.json, deliberately: that file is scoped
to the pre-114C MACHINE authorization surface (VALID_ROLES: dispatcher,
runner, observer, approver, reviewer) and its own every_baseline_role_is_a_valid_role
test would fail the moment 'admin' -- a human-only role, deliberately absent
from VALID_ROLES so no role token or the legacy bearer can ever hold it --
appeared in it. Account-administration routes get their own baseline
instead of weakening that self-consistency check to make room for them.
_route_comment: /accounts/{id}/membership and .../disable, .../enable are always ADMIN
regardless of method, checked before the generic GET-vs-mutation split.
/auth-policy, /auth/sessions*, /auth/logout, /auth/logout-all, /auth/me,
/auth/step-up/*, and /auth/passkeys/* are a coarse gate only (any
authenticated human, whatever role they hold -- SELF_SERVICE includes
admin/approver/dispatcher so a bootstrap admin is not locked out); the
handler enforces 'my own session(s)/account/passkey' using
AuthContext.human_principal -- required_roles() has no notion of
resource ownership, only role membership. Passkey register/remove are
also on the plan's step-up list (114C.6 Slice 4, not built yet) --
required_roles() has no notion of session assurance either, so this
coarse role gate is the only enforcement in place until then.
POST /auth/bootstrap, GET /auth/bootstrap/status, POST /auth/login, and
POST /auth/refresh are NOT listed here: they sit on the public router
tier (crate::routes::authn::public_router) and never reach
require_bearer/required_roles() at all -- a caller with no credential
yet cannot pass an authenticated-tier gate to obtain one.
The /settings routes live here rather than in role_policy_baseline.json
(the machine-surface fixture) because their policy now names the
human-only `admin` role, which that fixture's every_baseline_role_is_a
_valid_role guard rejects: settings reads admit observer/reviewer/admin,
and writes to the auth.* subtree (authentication policy -- admin
territory) admit admin/reviewer, resolving the first-admin passkey-setup
deadlock (114D groundwork). Every other settings key stays reviewer-only
(PUT /settings/thing above pins that default).
/admin/role-tokens* (2026-07-28 security fix): role-token *lifecycle*
mutation (issue/split/migrate/revoke) now requires `admin`, not merely
`reviewer` -- a bare reviewer-role token could previously mint itself a
fresh dispatcher/runner/approver/reviewer token, a privilege-escalation
path caught live during a 114C.8 drill re-run. Listing (GET) stays
reviewer-readable alongside admin, mirroring /accounts' identical
read/write split. The legacy bearer's own narrow three-path bootstrap
exception (auth.rs's is_authorized, not this route table) is untouched.
